title: saveRealFla drops flaSwfBlobs — the CPicSwf raw bytes the importer explicitly preserves 'for lossless re-export' are never re-emitted
description: The binary FLA importer captures every CPicSwf (embedded/imported SWF placement) record's raw bytes verbatim: flash8-binary.ts readCPicSwf:2467-2488 slices the whole undecoded record body into rawBytes, and flash8-import.ts collectSwfBlobs:1868-1889 + buildFla8Document:2130-2140 surface them on the document as doc.flaSwfBlobs, with comments promising 'lossless round-trip / a re-export can reproduce them; they are not lost' (flash8-import.ts:1193-1211). But the writer never reads that field: write/fla-write.ts saveRealFla:31-139 has no reference to flaSwfBlobs (its header even says 'CPicSwf is never emitted'), so importing a CS2-era FLA with embedded SWFs (e.g. fixtures/Magnet.fla, 4 instances) and re-saving via saveRealFla silently discards those placements — exactly the data-loss class the blobs were added to prevent. Why it matters: the flaSwfBlobs mechanism only earns its keep if the write path closes the loop; today the importer's comments are wrong and the model field is dead weight on the real-FLA save path (it IS synced by collab, task 1400). Fix: in saveRealFla/writeTimelineStream, re-emit each blob's raw record bytes into the timeline stream it came from (blobs carry sceneIndex; symbol-timeline blobs have sceneIndex undefined and need a symbol reference added at capture time), framed by a CPicSwf class tag via the ClassTable so the sec 5.2 running index stays consistent — or, if faithful re-framing proves infeasible (the blob starts at the record BODY, class tag excluded, and re-declaring CPicSwf changes downstream backref indices), decide + document that CPicSwf re-export is out of scope and fix the importer comments/model docs to stop claiming losslessness. Acceptance: round-trip test — feed a synthetic timeline containing a CPicSwf record through parseFla8Timeline -> buildFla8Document -> saveRealFla -> tryLoadRealFla and assert the blob bytes survive byte-identically (or the documented-scope alternative with comments corrected and a warning emitted on save when blobs are dropped).
